(1) 4,680 SNPs were identified in a core collection (150 accessions) of Chinese jujubes using genotyping-by-sequening (GBS); (2) the average polymorphism information contents (PICs) were 0.38 for tri-allelic and 0.27 for bi-allelic SNP markers, which indicated that the resolving power of tri-alleic SNPs was higher than that of bi-allelic ones; (3)
the resolving power of SNPs for genetic diversity and population structure was similar to that of SSRs in Chinese jujubes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a high-density genetic map and the identification of SNPs in Chinese jujubes, which will provide a valuable genetic resource for further studies of the genetic diversity, population genetics, and LD of Chinese jujubes.
the genetic diversity and population structure of Chinese jujubes, and it will provide valuable resources for the genetic improvement and conservation of Chinese jujubecultivars.
the development of high-quality SNPs for Chinese jujube, and provides a useful resource of genetic markers for future genetic and genomic studies in Chinese jujubes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resolving power of SNPs and SSRs for population structure is comparable.
the resolving power of SNPs and SSRs for genetic diversity was comparable, while the resolving power for population structure was higher for SSR markers than for SNPs.
the resolving power of the SSRs and the SNPs was similar, but the resolving power of SSRs was higher than that of the SNPs for population structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the core collection of Chinese jujubes was characterized with high genetic diversity, and the population structure was well defined with the combination of SSR and SNP markers.
SNPs developed by genotyping-by-sequening (GBS) are powerful tools for the analysis of genetic diversity, population structures, and linkage disequilbrium of jujube.
SNPs are more suitable for genetic diversity analysis and LD analysis, while SSRs are more suitable for population structure analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolving power of SSRs and SNPS for genetic diversity is similar, while the resolving power of the two markers for population structure is different.
the SNPs identified in this study are valuable for future studies of the genetic diversity of Chinese jujubes and for marker-assisted selection.
SNPs and SSRs are complementary in terms of their ability to detect genetic diversity and population structure.
